manual.hbm.satellite.xenrelay.title: Xenium Resonator Satellite
manual.hbm.satellite.xenrelay.content:
The xenium resonator allows teleportation within the same dimension. It can be controlled either with a satellite designator or the satellite laser designator. When using the satellite designator, the Y value can be omitted, which will default it to surface level.

{{Template:SatOverview}}
manual.hbm.weapon.ap.title: Armor Piercing Bullet
manual.hbm.weapon.ap.content:
AP rounds are similar to FMJ rounds, but using hardened steel jackets and significantly higher powder load. Not only do APs deal more damage and pierce through armor more effectively, but they can also penetrate their target.

{{Template:Bullet}}
manual.hbm.weapon.buckshot.title: Buckshot
manual.hbm.weapon.buckshot.content:
Standard shot, creates many low-damage pellets with considerable spread. Sometimes it's hard to beat the classics.

{{Template:Shotshells}}
manual.hbm.weapon.buckshotmagnum.title: Magnum Buckshot
manual.hbm.weapon.buckshotmagnum.content:
Buckshot, but with fewer larger pellets which deal more damage. While black powder magnum shells don't perform that much better compared to buckshot, smokeless powder ones are noticably more powerful. Additionally, magnum buckshot shells have roughly half as much spread as standard buckshot.

{{Template:Shotshells}}
manual.hbm.weapon.buckshotsharpnel.title: Shrapnel Buckshot
manual.hbm.weapon.buckshotsharpnel.conte:
A more devious version of standard buckshot, identical in most ways except that the pellets are incredibly bouncy, ricocheting off of most surfaces multiple times. May be hazardous to the user when used in enclosed spaces.

{{Template:Shotshells}}
manual.hbm.weapon.demo.title: Demolition Explosives
manual.hbm.weapon.demo.content:
Demolition explosives are similar to regular high-explosives, however they have a larger splash radius, slightly lower damage, and they break blocks. Not recommended for home defense.

{{Template:Explosives}}
manual.hbm.weapon.du.title: Depleted Uranium Bullet
manual.hbm.weapon.du.content:
Ammunition with depleted uranium in its core. The increased density and higher powder load causes this ammo type to have even better armor-piercing properties than AP ammo. The added punch causes the projectiles to penetrate.

Due to their intended effect being kinetic energy, rather than being poisonous, depleted uranium ammunition is not subject to the Hague Conventions of 1899 regarding use of poisonous projectiles in warfare.

{{Template:Bullet}}
{{Template:Shotshells}}
manual.hbm.weapon.express.title: FMJ Express Bullet
manual.hbm.weapon.express.content:
FMJ Express is a special type of full metal jacket ammo for revolver calibers. Express ammo has the same armor-piercing effects in addition to increased damage. Express projectiles can penetrate their targets, but unlike AP rounds, Express projectiles become weaker on every penetration. Due to the higher powder load in combination with the basic gunmetal casing, Express ammo causes the gun to wear faster.

{{Template:Bullet}}
manual.hbm.weapon.flechettes.title: Flechettes
manual.hbm.weapon.flechettes.content:
Flechettes are small fin-stabilized projectiles, contrary to buckshot's round pellets. Flechette shells have less spread and better armor-piercing compared to standard buckshot.

{{Template:Shotshells}}
manual.hbm.weapon.fmj.title: Full Metal Jacket Bullet
manual.hbm.weapon.fmj.content:
FMJs do not deform when hitting a soft target, meaning they deliver less damage. However, it allows them to pierce armor more effectively. All FMJs have some armor-piercing properties, as well as added damage threshold negation based on the caliber size.

{{Template:Bullet}}
manual.hbm.weapon.grenade.title: High-Explosives
manual.hbm.weapon.grenade.content:
Standard ammunition for grenade and rocket launchers. Deals splash damage in a moderate area.

{{Template:Explosives}}
manual.hbm.weapon.he.title: High-Explosive Ammunition
manual.hbm.weapon.he.content:
As one would expect, explosive ammunition deals explosive damage to its target, and the surroundings in a small radius. The resulting damage is noticably higher than the gun's base damage, at the cost of causing the gun to wear down significantly faster.

Use of explosive projectiles with a weight of less than 400 grams is prohibited by the Saint Petersburg Declaration of 1868.

{{Template:Bullet}}
{{Template:Shotshells}}
manual.hbm.weapon.heat.title: Shaped Charges
manual.hbm.weapon.heat.content:
Special type of explosive munition with weaker splash damage compared to high-explosives, which deals massive extra damage on direct hit.

{{Template:Explosives}}
manual.hbm.weapon.incendiary.title: Incendiary Munitions
manual.hbm.weapon.incendiary.content:
Incendiary explosives leave behind lingering fire, which can ignite targets. The afterburn does not last very long, and can be extinguished with water.

Use of incendiary weapons against or near civilians is forbidden by the Geneva Conventions.

{{Template:Explosives}}
manual.hbm.weapon.jhp.title: Jacketed Hollow Point Bullet
manual.hbm.weapon.jhp.content:
JHPs are deforming bullets that cause more damage to soft targets compared to soft point bullets, at the cost of faring worse against armored targets. JHPs also have a higher bonus on headshots.

Due to being expanding projectiles, jacketed hollow points are prohibited for use in warfare under the Hague Conventions of 1899.

manual.hbm.weapon.powder.title: Black Powder Ammunition
manual.hbm.weapon.powder.content:
The earliest available type of cartridge, black powder ammo is available for revolver calibers and 12 gauge shells. For revolver calibers, black powder bullets are a variant of soft point bullets. Black powder shells however are available in buckshot, magnum shot and slug variants. Black powder ammo is very cheap, but deals significantly less damage and causes a large cloud of smoke on every shot.

manual.hbm.weapon.slug.title: Slug
manual.hbm.weapon.slug.content:
A shell type that only holds a single large projectile. Unlike shot, slugs do not have inherent spread, deal the gun's full damage on hit, and have some armor-piercing properties.

{{Template:Shotshells}}
manual.hbm.weapon.softpoint.title: Soft Point Bullet
manual.hbm.weapon.softpoint.content:
The "default" ammunition type for most guns. Soft point bullets do not change the gun's base damage, and don't have any armor-piercing properties.

Due to being expanding projectiles, soft points are prohibited for use in warfare under the Hague Conventions of 1899.

{{Template:Bullet}}
manual.hbm.weapon.star.title: Starmetal Bullet
manual.hbm.weapon.star.content:
Cartridge with extra high powder load using a starmetal projectile. The density and stability of starmetal ensures that this projectile can punch through most armors, at the cost of the gun wearing ten times faster. Can only be used in anti-materiel rifles, as the chamber pressure is so high, it would blow automatic weapons apart.

manual.hbm.weapon.wp.title: White Phosphorus Munitions
manual.hbm.weapon.wp.content:
White phosphorus ignites easily and is very hard to extinguish, causing significant afterburn damage which cannot be permanently extinguished by water. Lingering fire caused by WP explosions lasts longer than by conventinal incendiary explosives.

Use of incendiary weapons against or near civilians is forbidden by the Geneva Conventions.
